purpose: Gap 12: neither SDK candidate has a retained same-task comparison preserving the required native account and recovery boundaries. This check installs the Claude Agent SDK into a fresh, version-pinned prefix separate from the wave-2 prefix, then runs the SAME frozen research task (blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/native-clients-research-task/task-prompt.txt, identical to the gap-2/8 check) through the Claude Agent SDK and through native `claude -p`, N=2 each, on the same account and Bash-only tool scope, plus one resume call per arm using a distinct follow-up prompt that requires recalling specific content from the first turn -- a genuine resume test, not a repeat of the same task.
preregistered: Frozen before any SDK/CLI run in this check, by file modification time (task-prompt.txt and resume-followup-prompt.txt were both written at 01:06:40 EDT, before sdk_run1's first output at 01:07:04): the same task-prompt.txt and rubric.json (reusing the gap-2/8 task and rubric), plus a new resume-followup-prompt.txt (blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/native-clients-research-task/) asking the model to restate the technique name and classify its own previous quantifiable number. CORRECTION (fix round): this follow-up question is a weaker continuity test than originally claimed. It is not 'answerable only by actually recalling the prior turn' -- resume-followup-prompt.txt itself offers the expected answer as one of three named choices ('a cache-read discount percentage, some other percentage, or a ratio/multiplier'), and it was authored (per its own mtime, 01:06:40) only after all six gap-2/8 outputs had already converged on exactly that answer, so a fresh session with no real continuity that simply re-derived the same generic, high-probability answer (as all 10 fresh runs in this unit did) would also pass this specific question. The original preregistered expectation ('a resume that silently starts a fresh context... would instead produce a generic or refused answer') is therefore not supported by this unit's own evidence and is retracted. Continuity for both arms is instead supported by stronger evidence recorded in raw_artifacts and cited in result: (1) the resumed call's session_id hashes identically to the originating run's session_id for both arms; (2) the CLI arm's cumulative usage fields arithmetically decompose into cli_run1 + cli_resume (e.g. output_tokens 697 = 587 + 110), which is only possible if the resume call was appended to the same server-side conversation state, not a fresh one; (3) the SDK resume call's cache_read_input_tokens (29201) equals sdk_run1's cache_creation_input_tokens (29201) exactly, consistent with the resume reading back the exact prefix sdk_run1 wrote; (4) each arm's resume answer recalled an arm-specific number that a generic re-derivation would not reliably reproduce (the SDK resume cites '2x for the 1-hour option', which appears only in sdk_run1's own answer; the CLI resume cites only '1.25x', matching cli_run1's own answer and omitting the 2x figure the SDK arm used) -- this cross-arm divergence in which specific tradeoff multiplier each resume cited is harder to explain by chance convergence than the shared 'cache-read discount percentage' framing. Usage and blind-judge quality (same rubric, same judge protocol as gap 2/8) are compared per arm on the 2 main runs only (the resume outputs are compared qualitatively for continuity, not re-judged on the R1-R3 quality rubric, since the resume prompt is a different, much shorter recall task) to keep this check's claude -p budget inside the unit's shared 16-call limit alongside gap 2/8.

Raw cli_resume.json's top-level total_cost_usd and modelUsage.costUSD are both 0.2074576, equal to cli_run1's own total_cost_usd (0.1795822) plus this call's own cost; the value recorded here (0.0278754) is that computed delta (0.2074576 - 0.1795822), not the raw cumulative field. The per-call token fields above (input/output/cache_creation/cache_read_input_tokens) are the raw JSON's top-level 'usage' object, which is per-call (not cumulative); the raw JSON's separate 'modelUsage' object IS cumulative and cross-checks against the delta: modelUsage.outputTokens 697 = cli_run1's 587 + this call's own 110; modelUsage.cacheReadInputTokens 74748 = cli_run1's 43091 + this call's own 31657.

result: The Claude Agent SDK, run through native Claude Code auth (no API key) with an allowed_tools=['Bash'] restriction and options.effort='medium', successfully completed the same frozen research task as native `claude -p` under matched settings, with the SDK's resume(=<prior session id>) option correctly continuing the same thread: the resumed SDK call's returned session id hashed identically to the original run's. Native `claude -p --resume <session-id>` showed the identical session-id-match pattern. CORRECTION (fix round): the resume-followup-prompt.txt question that both resume calls answered 'correctly' is a weaker continuity test than the original write-up implied -- it names the expected answer as one of three offered choices, was authored only after all six gap-2/8 outputs had already converged on that same answer, and all 10 fresh (non-resumed) runs in this unit gave the same answer, so a resume that silently started a fresh context would very plausibly also have 'passed' this specific question. Real continuity for both arms is instead established by usage-field evidence, not the follow-up answer alone: the CLI arm's raw cumulative modelUsage fields decompose exactly into cli_run1 + cli_resume (e.g. cumulative output_tokens 697 = 587 + 110), which requires server-side conversation continuity to produce; the SDK resume's cache_read_input_tokens (29201) equals sdk_run1's own cache_creation_input_tokens (29201) exactly, consistent with resume reading back the exact prefix sdk_run1 wrote; and each arm's resume answer cited an arm-specific number (SDK: '2x for the 1-hour option', appearing only in sdk_run1's own text; CLI: only '1.25x', matching cli_run1's own text and omitting the SDK arm's 2x figure) that a generic re-derivation would not reliably reproduce. Both arms therefore demonstrate working, verifiable same-thread resume with actual content continuity (not just a non-erroring resume flag, and not merely a guessable follow-up answer), on this account and tool scope -- this directly settles the 'SDK resume was previously only source-reviewed, never exercised' half of gap 12 noted in the wave-2 receipt's limitations. Quality: the blind judge scored all 4 main-run outputs (2 SDK, 2 CLI) 3/3, a ceiling effect consistent with the same finding on the same task in the gap-2/8 check -- a valid null result for this bounded task, not evidence the SDK and CLI paths are equivalent on harder tasks. Usage: the SDK's main-run mean output_tokens (585) and mean combined context (input+cache_creation+cache_read, ~55.7k) were close to claude -p's main-run mean output_tokens (575.5) and mean combined context (~62.97k); the SDK path's mean combined context was somewhat lower, but both CLI main runs' costs differed nearly 7x from each other (run 1 $0.180 vs run 2 $0.026) due to an apparent cache-warmth effect between the two back-to-back CLI calls, so a clean per-call cost comparison between the SDK and CLI paths is not reliable from N=2 with this much between-call variance. CORRECTION (fix round): the SDK path does not lack a native cost field in general -- the installed claude-agent-sdk 0.2.158's ResultMessage dataclass defines total_cost_usd: float | None (claude_agent_sdk/types.py). This check's own sdk-task.py harness script simply never read that field (it only recorded result, session_id, usage and is_error), so no SDK-arm dollar figure was captured this run; that is a gap in this check's harness script, not a property of the SDK, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact without re-running. Only claude -p's cost is reported here.

verdict_impact.explanation: Materially advances gap 12: it replaces the wave-2 receipt's source-review-only finding on SDK resume/session_id fields with an actually-exercised, same-task, matched-tool-scope comparison against native claude -p, including a resume continuity test for both arms corroborated by session-id and cumulative-usage evidence (not merely a non-erroring resume call, and not solely the follow-up question, which was itself a weaker test than originally claimed -- see result and limitations). Does not fully settle gap 12: quality is a ceiling-effect null result on this one bounded task (same caveat as gap 2/8), N=2 main runs per arm is small, the SDK path was not observed to report cost in this check because the harness script never read the SDK's existing total_cost_usd field (a harness gap, not a missing SDK capability), so no full cost comparison is possible from this run's evidence, and the observed ~7x cost swing between the CLI arm's own two back-to-back runs shows this task/account state is too cache-sensitive for a small-N cost comparison to be trusted without more trials or explicit cache-state control.

limitations: N=2 main runs + 1 resume per arm is small; the CLI arm's own two main runs differed in cost by nearly 7x due to an apparent cache-warmth effect between back-to-back calls, so per-call cost/usage means reported here should be read as indicative, not precise, at this N.

CORRECTION (fix round): the claude -p (resume, N=1) total_cost_usd figure in model_calls (0.0278754) is a computed delta, not a raw field -- claude -p's total_cost_usd on a --resume call reports the CUMULATIVE cost of the whole resumed session (0.2074576 in the raw cli_resume.json), not the resume call's own cost; the delta was computed by subtracting cli_run1's own total_cost_usd (0.1795822). This was caught and corrected in a fix round after the initial receipt mistakenly reported the raw cumulative field as the resume call's own cost.

CORRECTION (fix round): this check's own sdk-task.py harness script did not read the SDK ResultMessage's existing total_cost_usd field, so no SDK-arm dollar figure was captured; this is a gap in this check's harness (fixable in a future run), not evidence the SDK lacks a native cost field. The initial receipt incorrectly stated the SDK 'exposes no native total_cost_usd field at all'; that claim is retracted.

Quality is a ceiling-effect null result (all 4 judged outputs scored 3/3 on the same rubric as gap 2/8, for the same reason: this bounded recall task was not hard enough to discriminate quality). This does not establish SDK/CLI quality equivalence on harder or more open-ended tasks.

CORRECTION (fix round): the resume follow-up prompt's own 'correct answer' cannot by itself distinguish real resume from a fresh session that happened to re-derive the same common answer (it offers the expected answer as one of three named choices, and was authored after all six gap-2/8 fresh runs had already converged on that answer; all 10 fresh runs in this unit gave the same answer). The follow-up prompt was judged only qualitatively for correct-recall-vs-generic-answer (both arms passed), not re-scored on the R1-R3 rubric; the stronger continuity evidence for this check's 'partially settles' verdict is the session-id match, the CLI arm's cumulative-usage arithmetic, the SDK arm's cache-token match, and each arm's arm-specific number recall (see result), not the follow-up prompt's pass/fail alone.

Only one resume hop was tested per arm (a single follow-up turn); multi-hop resume chains, resume after a long delay, resume across a host restart, or resume of a session that hit a tool-permission denial are not tested here.

The SDK was exercised through this check's own minimal script (options.effort='medium', allowed_tools=['Bash'], resume=<id>); it does not exercise MCP tools, hooks, subagents, or other SDK surface area beyond what the wave-2 receipt already covered as install/single-tool-call evidence.

CORRECTION (fix round): this check's own CLI arm ran with cwd=~/code/nas-wt-w3-native-clients and 47 available tools (confirmed from the raw system/init events), matching this check's intended scope. However, the reused task-prompt.txt and rubric.json were also used by the separate gap-2/8 check (arm-comparison-research-task.json), whose claude -p arm and all judge calls instead ran with cwd=~/code/agent-lab and 124 available tools (bypassPermissions, including WebFetch/WebSearch/MCP servers) -- see the correction recorded in that receipt. This check's own SDK-vs-CLI comparison is internally consistent (both its arms ran in the same worktree at the same tool count), but a reader should not treat this check's usage/context figures as directly comparable to the gap-2/8 claude -p arm's figures, since the two checks' claude -p runs did not share the same tool-availability environment despite sharing the same prompt text.

This unit stopped all further claude -p and SDK calls after this check: five_hour rate-limit utilization on the shared account had climbed to allowed_warning 0.96 by the last judge call (never reaching a 429/blocked state, so no calls were abandoned mid-run), and the unit's own 16-call claude -p budget (judge calls included, shared with gap 2/8) was exactly exhausted by this point; both are recorded here as the reason no additional SDK/CLI trials were attempted, not as an error.
